Seventeen comments

Wolfstone

I think this tune is an amazing tune. I was searching for it and found loads of submissions but they certainly were not the Richard Dwyers i learnt. This is the reel played by wolfstone in the ‘dinner set’ on they’re ‘Year of the Dog’ Album.

I get very frustrated with the number of names some tunes are given and also names used repeatedly for different tunes, this seems to be a perfect example. There is already a jig and a reel here that are clearly different tunes.

This is my first tune submission so i hope i did the tune justice.

↳ Posted by fiddlematt on April 17th, 2008.

Doubt it…

I can’t remember where or who at the moment, but I’ve heard this before, and am pretty sure it’s a recent composition, possibly Scottish, and nothing to do with Richard Dwyer. Just doesn’t sound like his style of tune.

↳ Posted by Kenny on April 17th, 2008.

Fair Enough

↳ Posted by Thomas Foschini on April 4th, 2021.

Re: Richard Dwyer’s

I’ve just heard this tune played on BBC Alba by the Field Marshall Montgomery Pipe Band in their winning selection from the World Pipe Band Championships in 2018. They have been playing this tune for years, I’m sure I have heard them play it maybe 10 - 15 years ago. What has been hinted at, but no one has actually suggested is that there may very probably be another composer of tunes by the name of Richard Dwyer, rather than the Co. Cork composer of many fine tunes we’re familiar with here.
Jarlath Henderson has been booked for the Tradition Bearers Concert at Stonehaven Folk Festival next weekend, as a singer, rather than instrumentalist, and very well deserved in my opinion. If I get a chance, I’ll ask him where he got the tune from - although the answer may well be Ross Ainslie, in which case, we’re back to square one.

↳ Posted by Kenny on July 1st, 2022.

Richard Dwyer’s, X:5

Here’s the setting of Field Marshall Montgomery mentioned by Kenny, above. In their medley, they only play the first part once but I’ve put a repeat in to make it less of an “arrangement”. I’ve also notated all the crotchet ornaments as plain triplets.
You can hear their setting from the 2018 Worlds here:
